title: @nrouter/sdk is not on npm
detail: README advertises `npm install @nrouter/sdk`; registry.npmjs.org returns 404.
impact: The documented install command fails for every user who tries it.
suggested_fix: Publish per sdks/js (npm publish --access public), or keep the README's not-published marker until then.
verified_how: curl registry.npmjs.org/@nrouter%2Fsdk -> 404 on 2026-08-26

title: ai.nrouter:nrouter-sdk-kotlin is not on Maven Central
detail: Only ai.nrouter:nrouter-sdk (the Java SDK) exists under the ai.nrouter group.
impact: Kotlin consumers cannot resolve the artifact; Android cannot resolve its dependency either.
suggested_fix: Follow sdks/kotlin/PUBLISHING.md. The ai.nrouter namespace is already verified since the Java SDK ships from it.
verified_how: repo1.maven.org/maven2/ai/nrouter/ lists only nrouter-sdk/

title: ai.nrouter:nrouter-sdk-android is not on Maven Central
detail: Depends on SDK-002: the AAR names ai.nrouter:nrouter-sdk-kotlin, which is not public.
impact: Publishing Android first would ship an AAR whose POM names an unresolvable dependency.
suggested_fix: Publish the Kotlin core first and confirm it resolves from Central, then Android. Ordering rule is in sdks/android/PUBLISHING.md.
verified_how: repo1.maven.org listing; sdks/android/build.gradle.kts api() coordinate

title: The Swift package has no semver tag, so it cannot be resolved yet
detail: SwiftPM resolves a git repo by tag and reads Package.swift from the repository ROOT. Both are now satisfied: a root Package.swift ships from this SDK tree (the public repo root) with path: targets into sdks/swift/. The public repo has NO tags, so `from: "2.1.0"` resolves nothing.
impact: Swift consumers cannot depend on the package until a tag exists.
suggested_fix: Publish the subtree split, then push a bare semver tag (2.1.0, no `v`) to the PUBLIC repo. Steps in sdks/swift/PUBLISHING.md. A separate nrouter-sdk-swift repo is NOT needed — that was an earlier wrong conclusion, now corrected.
verified_how: git ls-remote --tags nrouter-sdk -> empty. Root-manifest approach proven end to end in .scratch: fixture repo + tag + a consumer package resolved, built and RAN against it.

title: The nrouter crate is not on crates.io
detail: README advertises `cargo add nrouter`; the crates.io API returns 404 for the name.
impact: The documented install command fails. The name is also unclaimed, so someone else could take it.
suggested_fix: Publish per sdks/rust/PUBLISHING.md. Claiming the name early is worth doing even ahead of a full release.
verified_how: crates.io/api/v1/crates/nrouter -> 404 (an earlier 403 was a user-agent block, not an answer)

title: The nrouter package is not on pub.dev
detail: README advertises `dart pub add nrouter`; pub.dev returns 404.
impact: The documented install command fails.
suggested_fix: Publish per sdks/dart/PUBLISHING.md. Consider a verified publisher for nrouter.ai at the same time.
verified_how: pub.dev/api/packages/nrouter -> 404

title: The R package is on neither R-universe nor CRAN
detail: nrouterai.r-universe.dev returns 404 for the package.
impact: The documented install command fails; only install_github works today.
suggested_fix: R-universe first (no review queue, builds binaries). CRAN only once the API is settled.
verified_how: nrouterai.r-universe.dev/api/packages/nrouter -> 404

title: No SDK has ever been run against the live gateway
detail: Every wire test uses a mock server or a stub transport. Nothing here proves the gateway accepts what these SDKs send.
impact: A wrong header name, auth shape or body field would pass every test and fail on the first real call.
suggested_fix: Run one chat completion per SDK against api.nrouter.ai with a real key and assert the x-nr-* headers come back. Cheapest possible smoke: 1 token, 9 calls.
verified_how: grep for a live base URL in tests: none; all use MockWebServer/MockClient/StubProtocol/TcpListener

title: The Java SDK exposes no x-nr-* metadata and no typed errors
detail: Zero occurrences of 'x-nr-' in sdks/java. It is a thin wrapper over com.openai:openai-java and inherits that SDK's errors.
impact: Java users cannot read per-request cost, tokens or cache outcome, and cannot distinguish a guardrail block from a malformed request.
suggested_fix: Add an OkHttp interceptor that captures the x-nr-* headers, plus the same 9-code classifier the native SDKs share.
verified_how: grep -c 'x-nr-' sdks/java/src/main/java/ai/nrouter/sdk/NRouter.java -> 0

title: The JS SDK exposes no x-nr-* metadata helper and no typed errors
detail: Zero occurrences of 'x-nr-' in sdks/js/src. Cost is reachable only by calling .asResponse() by hand.
impact: JS users get no typed error hierarchy and no ergonomic cost access, unlike the five native SDKs.
suggested_fix: Add a ResponseMeta parser and the shared 9-code classifier, mirroring sdks/kotlin.
verified_how: grep -c 'x-nr-' sdks/js/src/client.ts -> 0

title: No native SDK supports streaming (stream: true / SSE)
detail: The JSON helpers refuse a non-JSON response and bytes() returns the whole body once complete. Neither yields incremental tokens.
impact: Streaming is the default UX for chat. Today a caller must either wait for the full response or parse SSE themselves.
suggested_fix: Add an SSE reader per SDK returning a stream/flow/sequence of deltas. Note the gateway does not response-cache streaming requests.
verified_how: grep for SSE/text-event-stream parsing in each SDK source: only comments, no parser

title: R has no request-path tests
detail: Its 77 assertions cover classification, metadata parsing and key redaction, but nothing exercises an actual HTTP send. No local server package is installed.
impact: A regression in nrouter_request/nrouter_multipart URL building, auth header or response handling would not be caught.
suggested_fix: Add webfakes to Suggests and write the same request-path tests the other SDKs have.
verified_how: requireNamespace('webfakes'/'httptest2') -> FALSE; no server used in tests/testthat

title: Swift has no cancellation test
detail: Kotlin proves a cancelled caller cancels the in-flight call. URLSession cancellation via async/await is not asserted anywhere in Swift.
impact: A cancelled Swift caller could leave a billed request running, the same defect that was real in Kotlin.
suggested_fix: Assert that cancelling the enclosing Task aborts the URLSessionTask, using the existing StubProtocol harness.
verified_how: grep -i cancel sdks/swift/Tests -> no match

title: No CI runs any of these suites
detail: The only workflow present is amp-ci.yml.disabled. GitHub Actions is also unavailable for this org (no runners plus a billing hold).
impact: Nine suites across six toolchains are only ever run by hand. A regression lands silently.
suggested_fix: Either restore Actions billing/runners, or add a single local script that runs all nine and is invoked before each release.
verified_how: ls .github/workflows -> amp-ci.yml.disabled only

title: The conformance gate cannot bind each error code to ITS status
detail: It requires every spec status to appear in a dispatch, but moving invalid_request from 400 to 503 leaves the set unchanged and passes.
impact: An error contract could drift in the spec while the gate stays green.
suggested_fix: Needs real parsing per language, not text matching. Meanwhile each SDK's own mutation-checked code-to-type tests cover it. A proximity heuristic was tried and produced six false positives; do not re-add it.
verified_how: Documented in conformance/README.md and in check_conformance.py

title: The conformance gate proves a constant is used, not used correctly
detail: The declared-and-used rule catches a deleted parser lookup, but an SDK could still read a header into the wrong field.
impact: A silently mis-wired header would pass the cross-SDK gate.
suggested_fix: Covered per SDK by its metadata parsing tests. Closing it in the gate needs execution, not text.
verified_how: Documented in conformance/README.md

title: The Rust MSRV is 1.88, which is high for a client library
detail: The floor comes from the transitive graph (icu_* via reqwest's TLS stack), not from this crate's own code.
impact: Consumers on an older toolchain cannot use the SDK at all.
suggested_fix: Try rustls-free or older-pinned feature sets for reqwest and re-measure. Derive the floor with the cargo metadata one-liner in PUBLISHING.md; never lower the field without `cargo +<v> check --locked`.
verified_how: cargo metadata: max rust_version across the graph = 1.88; cargo +1.75.0 check --locked fails

title: Swift multipart encoding is hand-rolled
detail: URLSession ships no multipart builder, so the body is assembled by hand. Quoted-string escaping and CR/LF stripping are covered by a test, but the encoder is bespoke.
impact: Any future edit risks re-opening the header-injection hole that was already found and fixed once.
suggested_fix: Keep the injection test as the guard. Consider a small vetted encoder if the surface grows.
verified_how: sdks/swift/Sources/NRouter/NRouter.swift multipart(); injection test present

title: The Android build needs an Android SDK that is not part of this repo
detail: Built locally against command-line tools fetched into .scratch; ANDROID_HOME or local.properties must point at an install.
impact: Anyone cloning fresh cannot build the AAR without that setup, and it is not scripted.
suggested_fix: Document the exact sdkmanager packages in sdks/android/PUBLISHING.md, or script the fetch.
verified_how: gradle build fails with 'SDK location not found' until ANDROID_HOME is set

title: R CMD check --as-cran reports two NOTEs
detail: 'New submission' (true, and clears after the first acceptance) and 'pandoc not installed' (environmental).
impact: Neither is a defect, but CRAN submission will surface both and a reviewer will ask.
suggested_fix: Install pandoc to clear the second locally. The first resolves itself on acceptance.
verified_how: R CMD check --as-cran -> Status: 2 NOTEs, both named above

title: Python has no bytes() or multipart helpers
detail: It wraps the OpenAI SDK, which handles both internally, so /v1/audio/* work — but there is no nRouter-branded helper and no test proving the audio endpoints are reachable.
impact: Parity gap versus the five native SDKs, and the audio path is unproven for Python.
suggested_fix: Either add thin helpers or add a test asserting the vendor client reaches /v1/audio/transcriptions.
verified_how: grep for multipart/bytes in sdks/python -> no match

title: verify-layout.sh has one pre-existing failure: agents/hermes-agent
detail: Present on origin/main before this SDK work; left by the earlier removal of the vendored NousResearch/hermes-agent.
impact: The repo's own layout guard is never fully green, which trains people to ignore it.
suggested_fix: Either restore the path or drop it from the expected-layout list in scripts/verify-layout.sh.
verified_how: Reproduced on a clean origin/main worktree: 1 FAIL, this one

title: No script publishes to the public nrouter-sdk repo
detail: scripts/publish-sdk-subtree.sh is named 'publish' and its last line is `git push -f origin sdk-only` — origin being the AUTHORING repo (nrouter-ent-ai-hub). Updating nRouterAI/nrouter-sdk is a separate manual push that no script performs, and the split branch has NO shared ancestry with public main (git merge-base is empty), so it rewrites that history.
impact: The public repo silently lags the authoring repo — it is missing everything in this SDK work today. It also means a release can tag a stale tree; for Swift that mints an immutable tag with no root Package.swift, unusable and unfixable. And the manual push can destroy outside contributions merged on public main.
suggested_fix: Either extend the script with an explicit, confirmed second push to the public remote plus a check that nothing on public main is unrepresented in the split, or rename it so it stops reading as a publish. Documented meanwhile in sdks/swift/PUBLISHING.md step 2.
verified_how: Read scripts/publish-sdk-subtree.sh (final line pushes to origin); git merge-base origin/sdk-only <public main> returns empty

title: nrouter-app still points at the SDK's old home inside nrouter-ent-ai-hub
detail: The SDK became its own repo on 2026-08-26. nrouter-app was NOT updated because a live session was editing it at the time (Rule #32). One FUNCTIONAL reference: tests/guards/sdk-error-classes-exist.sh defaults SDK_ERRORS to $APP_ROOT/../nrouter-ent-ai-hub/nrouter-sdk/sdks/python. The rest are comments in src/app/api/openapi/route.ts, src/lib/playground/code-generators.ts, src/lib/super-admin/provider-schema/types.ts and src/data/api-reference/api-contract.ts.
impact: The guard degrades safely — it exits 78 (SKIP LOUDLY) when the path is missing, so nothing silently passes — but it no longer RUNS, so the contract that every error class the API reference names actually exists in the Python SDK is unverified.
suggested_fix: Change the default to $APP_ROOT/../nrouter-sdk/sdks/python (the NROUTER_SDK_ROOT override already works and needs no change), and refresh the four comments. Do it when no session is live in nrouter-app.
verified_how: grep for ent-ai-hub in nrouter-app; guard read at tests/guards/sdk-error-classes-exist.sh; exit-78 skip path confirmed in its source

title: The Go module is not tagged, so go get cannot resolve it
detail: Go has no registry: proxy.golang.org serves whatever a git tag points at, and a module in a subdirectory needs the subdirectory-prefixed tag sdks/go/vX.Y.Z. No such tag exists.
impact: The documented install command fails, and it fails as module not found — which reads like a network problem rather than an unpublished package.
suggested_fix: Tag per sdks/go/PUBLISHING.md from a clean pushed main. A bare vX.Y.Z tag resolves the repo ROOT, which is not a Go module, and will not work.
verified_how: git tag -l sdks/go/* -> empty; go.mod declares github.com/nRouterAI/nrouter-sdk/sdks/go
